newsitem.title: GERMANY: U.S. soldier in Germany to face sex charges trial.
newsitem.headline: U.S. soldier in Germany to face sex charges trial.

text.p: A U.S. army sergeant accused of raping and sodomising female soldiers at a training base in Germany will face a general court-martial hearing next week, the U.S. army's European headquarters said on Wednesday.

The soldier, Sergeant First Class Julius Davis of the 440th Signal Battalion based in Darmstadt, Germany, will face trial beginning on June 2 on charges that include six counts of rape and one count of forced sodomy.

The court-martial panel, the military version of a civilian trial's jury, will be selected on Friday for the hearing at the Darmstadt training centre, which is located about 30 km (20 miles) south of Frankfurt and and which is where the alleged crimes were said to have taken place.

The hearing is the latest scandal hit the army as it probes incidents at training bases in the United States and Germany where a number of male sergeants have been alleged to have harassed, raped and sodomised women soldiers.
The army has also suspended its top enlisted man, Sergeant Major of the Army Gene McKinney, from duty in Washington pending resolution of sexual harassment charges against him.
Davis, 37, from Fayetteville, North Carolina, has been held at a military prision in Mannheim since early February when allegations first surfaced of sexual misconduct.
Another soldier, Sergeant Paul Fuller of the 77th Maintenance Company in Babenhausen, Germany, faces charges including three counts of rape and three counts of sodomy.
The court-martial hearing for Fuller, 26 of Columbus, Ohio, is scheduled to begin on June 9, the army said.

A third sergeant has been accused of illegal fraternisation with a lower-ranking soldier at the base where at least 21 female soldiers have come forward to make allegations against the men who were supervisors on a six-month rotation.
The incidents were alleged to have taken place between November and January at the centre where new soldiers arriving for duty in the Darmstadt area spend two weeks in an orientation programme.
The army has replaced the male commander of the centre with a woman.
